title: Nancy Guthrie Investigation Data Recovery (Google LLC / Nest Labs)

communications.communication:
VIA ELECTRONIC TRANSMISSION

TO: Record/Information Dissemination Section (RIDS)
Federal Bureau of Investigation
170 Marcel Drive
Winchester, VA 22602-4843

RE: Freedom of Information Act Request — Nancy Guthrie Investigation Data Recovery (Google LLC / Nest Labs)

I. Statutory Standing and Jurisdiction
Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act (“FOIA”), 5 U.S.C. § 552 et seq., and the implementing regulations of the United States Department of Justice, 28 C.F.R. Part 16, this correspondence constitutes a formal request for agency records. As a member of the public, the requester possesses statutory standing to compel the disclosure of the aforementioned records, subject only to the narrowly construed statutory exemptions enumerated in 5 U.S.C. § 552(b).

II. Definitions and Rules of Construction
For the purposes of this request, the following definitions and rules of construction shall apply:

“Record” or “Records” shall be construed in the broadest possible sense to include any “agency record” within the meaning of 5 U.S.C. § 552(f)(2). This encompasses, without limitation, all documents, memoranda, electronic communications (including emails, SMS messages, secure messaging applications, and internal chat platforms), physical and electronic files, drafts, notes, calendar entries, audio/video recordings, metadata, database exports, and any other compilation of data, regardless of physical form or characteristics, currently in the possession, custody, or control of the Federal Bureau of Investigation (“FBI”).

“Communication” means the transmittal or receipt of information (in the form of facts, ideas, inquiries, or otherwise), regardless of the medium or method of transmission.

“Google” or “Nest” refers collectively and individually to Google LLC, Alphabet Inc., Nest Labs, their subsidiaries, affiliates, officers, directors, employees, legal counsel, technical engineers, and any third-party agents operating on their behalf.

“Concerning” means relating to, referring to, describing, evidencing, constituting, or reflecting the stated subject matter, either directly or indirectly.

Words used in the singular shall include the plural, and vice versa. The conjunctions “and” and “or” shall be construed both conjunctively and disjunctively to ensure the broadest possible interpretation of the request.

III. Records Requested
The requester hereby demands the production of all records and communications concerning the FBI’s request for, preservation, recovery, receipt, acquisition, processing, or subsequent handling of video or associated data obtained from Google concerning cameras situated at or associated with the residence of Nancy Guthrie.

The time period of this request is restricted to records created, modified, or received between February 1, 2026, and February 11, 2026, inclusive.

This request specifically includes, inter alia:

All communications between any agent, employee, or representative of the FBI and any personnel or representative of Google regarding the Guthrie investigation.

All preservation letters, search warrants, subpoenas (including grand jury and administrative subpoenas), court orders, exigent/emergency requests, or other compulsory legal process served upon or transmitted to Google.

All records concerning technical, operational, or forensic efforts, methodologies, or collaborations between Google and the FBI to locate, reconstruct, extract, recover, decrypt, or otherwise produce the requested data.

All production letters, data manifests, digital inventories, receipts, chain-of-custody documentation, or other transmittal records identifying the files, datasets, or metadata provided to or obtained by the FBI from Google.

All records concerning the FBI’s internal receipt, review, processing, redaction, and subsequent public dissemination of the recovered photographs or video.

IV. Preclusion of Exemptions via Official Public Acknowledgment
The FBI is precluded from issuing a Glomar response (refusing to confirm or deny the existence of records) or claiming blanket exemption over these materials under 5 U.S.C. § 552(b)(7)(A) (interference with law enforcement proceedings), as the core facts of this inquiry have been officially acknowledged.

Under the "Official Acknowledgment" doctrine, an agency waives its right to withhold information that has already been publicly disclosed by an authorized official. See Wolf v. CIA, 473 F.3d 370, 378 (D.C. Cir. 2007); Afshar v. Dep't of State, 702 F.2d 1125, 1133 (D.C. Cir. 1983).

On February 10, 2026, the FBI affirmatively published photographs and video recovered in this investigation, confirming the footage depicted an armed individual tampering with a camera at the Guthrie residence (Reference: https://www.fbi.gov/news/RSS?PQZbxSJnkbv=G43cDa). Furthermore, FBI Director Kash Patel publicly and officially confirmed that this imagery was recovered via cooperation with private-sector partners from “residual data located in backend systems.” Extensive, verified reporting corroborated this specific partnership, detailing Google engineers’ multi-day forensic recovery of the Nest camera data (References: CNN Transcripts, CBS News).

Because the FBI’s relationship with Google, the deployment of legal process, and the successful recovery of this data are matters of public record established by the FBI Director, this request does not seek to uncover undisclosed investigative techniques or unacknowledged partnerships.

V. Standards for Adequacy of Search and Segregability
The FBI is legally obligated to conduct a search “reasonably calculated to uncover all relevant documents.” Weisberg v. U.S. Dep't of Justice, 705 F.2d 1344, 1351 (D.C. Cir. 1983). This search must include all electronic systems, investigative files, legal-process repositories, and databases utilized by the components involved in the Guthrie investigation.

To the extent the FBI determines that any responsive record contains exempt material, the FBI must disclose all reasonably segregable, non-exempt portions pursuant to 5 U.S.C. § 552(b). See Mead Data Cent., Inc. v. U.S. Dep't of the Air Force, 566 F.2d 242, 260 (D.C. Cir. 1977). The agency may not withhold records in their entirety if administrative, technical, procedural, legal-process, or already-publicly-acknowledged details can be severed from protected investigative details.

For any material withheld, the FBI must expressly identify the applicable statutory exemption and provide a sufficiently detailed Vaughn index to permit independent review of the withholding. See Vaughn v. Rosen, 484 F.2d 820 (D.C. Cir. 1973). Consistent with the FOIA Improvement Act of 2016, 5 U.S.C. § 552(a)(8)(A), the agency may only withhold information if it “reasonably foresees that disclosure would harm an interest protected by an exemption.” See Reporters Comm. for Freedom of the Press v. FBI, 3 F.4th 350, 369 (D.C. Cir. 2021).

VI. Format of Production
Pursuant to 5 U.S.C. § 552(a)(3)(B), I request that all records be produced in their native electronic format, preserving all original metadata, or in a standard searchable PDF format. Please transmit the responsive records electronically to the undersigned.

VII. Application for Fee Waiver and Public Interest Disclosure
Pursuant to 5 U.S.C. § 552(a)(4)(A)(iii) and 28 C.F.R. § 16.10(k), the requester formally applies for a complete waiver or reduction of all search, review, and duplication fees. Disclosure of the requested records is in the public interest because it is “likely to contribute significantly to public understanding of the operations or activities of the government and is not primarily in the commercial interest of the requester.”

1. Significant Contribution to Public Understanding
The operations of the FBI—specifically regarding the acquisition, preservation, and forensic extraction of private-sector cloud data (such as Google/Nest backend systems) during a high-profile missing persons investigation—constitute matters of profound public importance.

Extensive Public Media Coverage: This case has generated intense national media scrutiny, featured prominently across major networks and news organizations, including CNN and CBS News.

Official Government Statements: Public interest has been directly stimulated by official disclosures from high-ranking government officials, including FBI Director Kash Patel’s public statements concerning private-sector cooperation and the recovery of residual data.

Filling an Informational Void: While initial news reports have summarized the broad strokes of the collaboration between federal law enforcement and Google engineers, the public lacks a comprehensive, verified understanding of the formal legal processes, technical methodologies, and operational timelines utilized. Disclosure will significantly advance the public’s comprehension of how law enforcement interacts with digital infrastructure and private communication platforms in active investigations.

2. Absence of Commercial Interest
The requester is an individual seeking these records for non-commercial purposes (e.g., public accountability, journalism, or educational research). The requester has no commercial interest in the release of these records, and disclosure will not yield any commercial gain. The primary objective is to contribute to an informed public discourse concerning transparency, digital evidence recovery, and federal law enforcement practices.

Accordingly, a waiver of all applicable fees is fully warranted under the statutory criteria.
